shortlist.selectionReason: Best fit for a calm SaaS hero where the proof artifact is visible before the fold.
Competitor matrix maps directly to Five to Nine's watchlist/change comparison job.
Alert list and timestamps map to proof-backed monitoring and digest triggers.
Report-led hero framing supports the morning-brief product story.
Simple analytics artifact keeps truth and status labels understandable.
Dark monitoring mood supports the after-hours story if kept readable and restrained.
Marketing-team dashboard plus social proof architecture fits the audience without copying claims.
Typographic growth energy is useful for a bolder territory, with claims toned down for pilot truth.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Lead database signup and review claims do not map to Five to Nine's current launch truth.
Photo-led service software composition fights the proof-backed monitoring product job.
Consumer testimonial grid encourages unsupported proof and weakens SaaS credibility.
Generic generated landing-page structure is exactly the pattern the proving lab must reject.

business-job: Make pilot credibility obvious before the fold.
content-strategy: Lead with what changed, with proof.
Use pilot-access CTA, not self-serve checkout.
Use source labels as trust-building UI.
voice-and-tone: No inflated security/compliance or launch claims.
typography: Dense but readable artifact labels from Profound/Amplitude.
Avoid tiny low-contrast dashboard text on mobile.
layout-structure: Proof artifact centered or split with hero copy.
Artifact should feel like the product, not decoration.
Use a sticky disciplined nav only if it does not crowd mobile.
spacing-system: Wide first fold with enough breathing room.
Compact proof rows in artifact surfaces.
Mobile uses stacked cards and sticky CTA.
responsive-behavior: Mobile first two screens must show headline, pilot truth, CTA, and proof artifact.
Do not bury the source-status boundary below pricing.
color-system: Dark direction must use accessible text contrast.
surfaces-and-materials: Dashboard glass is allowed only when labels remain readable.
Paper/report surfaces fit the morning brief story.
Dark cinematic surfaces must still feel operational.
depth: Use depth to separate proof receipts from background.
No decorative floating cards without information value.
shape: Rounded chips only for status labels and source states.
component-anatomy: Hero proof artifact, source chip, watchlist row, alert row, morning brief card, pricing/pilot panel.
component-states: Live, cached, degraded, demo states must be visually distinct.
Beta and pilot statuses need visible labels.
interaction-model: Primary action enters pilot or opens workspace.
motion: Motion can imply overnight scanning but must not hide content.
Cinematic direction can use scroll reveal later; concept proof stays static.
media-direction: Use product-like proof artifacts, not generic photos.
Avoid fake customer logos unless sourced.
iconography: Use simple signal, receipt, watchlist, source, and brief symbols.
illustration-graphics: Allowed as gridlines, timelines, and signal paths.
Reject abstract blobs with no product meaning.
proof-architecture: Proof is source, timestamp, status, confidence, and recommended next action.
Mobbin references are design proof, not product proof.
cta-system: Tertiary: Read pilot truth or launch state.
forms-and-lead-capture: Pilot access should feel deliberate and fit-reviewed.
accessibility: Mobile status chips need legible sizes.
localization-and-formatting: India-first examples can mention COD, Nykaa, Meesho, boAt only as demo/sample context.
Do not imply current live monitoring of those brands unless proof exists.
seo-aeo-metadata: Keep agent-readable truth aligned with visible page: pilot-readiness, beta tracking, no live checkout.
performance: Use CSS and product artifacts, not heavy video for the first fold.
WebGL style can be deferred until product truth is stronger.
implementation-tokens: Accent should be a product signal token, not random brand flourish.
Status colors must map to source truth states.
governance: Any final build needs browser screenshots, source-status copy review, and no-unsupported-claim check.

compatibilityDecision: Best coherent direction is proof-led data minimalism with one bolder editorial or dark variant as a challenger. The strongest shared ingredient is a real product artifact that makes source status and morning brief value visible before the fold.
